The case has directly affected her and her family, prompting her to describe feeling as though she could finally breathe again after seven years of advocacy. Guardian journalist Kaamil Ahmed explains in a podcast how the case unfolded and what consequences may follow. Ullah notes that the verdict could have far-reaching implications for Israel, which is also facing a genocide case at the ICJ.
items.title: Myanmar Found Guilty of Genocide Against Rohingya; Podcast Examines Implications for Israel

items.summary: At a United Nations Security Council briefing on Monday, India's Permanent Representative Harish Parvathaneni called for an immediate end to attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Black Sea, stressing that safe navigation through international waterways must be restored amid the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Addressing the high-level session, Ambassador Parvathaneni said the war, now in its fifth year, has far-reaching consequences due to interconnected global supply chains, noting India's readiness to contribute to efforts toward a peaceful resolution and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for moving from 'endless war to the end of war.' He highlighted that armed conflicts disrupt agriculture, displace communities, damage infrastructure, and hinder humanitarian access, with consequences extending globally through disruptions to energy, fertiliser, transport, and agricultural trade while disproportionately impacting the Global South. Parvathaneni emphasized the Security Council's need to prioritise humanitarian access, protection of civilian infrastructure, and freedom of navigation so that humanitarian supplies and legitimate trade are not affected. He underscored the Black Sea region's importance to global food security, noting it and India together account for almost a fifth of global cereal production, while Russia and Ukraine combined accounted for nearly a quarter of global exports of wheat, maize, and barley. The Indian envoy cited India's humanitarian assistance—wheat supplies to Afghanistan, rice to Sudan, and aid to Palestine—and stressed that the Global South is disproportionately affected by food, fuel, and fertiliser crises from conflicts, with energy shortages intensifying concerns; he referenced External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's observation at last month's G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting that fertiliser shortages stem partly from the Black Sea and partly from the Gulf and Red Sea. Parvathaneni recalled the 1943 Bengal famine, which killed over three million people in India, as a reminder of distant conflicts' devastating human costs. He detailed attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea involving four ships: MV Omorfi (attacked July 18), MV Royad Mammadov (October), and MV Golden Leo and MV AGN RAGNAR, resulting in four dead and two missing Indian seafarers; he thanked partner countries for repatriating injured seafarers. Parvathaneni called for an end to targeting commercial shipping and restoration of safe navigation through international waterways at the earliest, noting India's efforts to strengthen maritime safety cooperation, including launching the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers with Liberia during earlier this month's UN high-level week. The voluntary mechanism supports the International Maritime Organisation and International Labour Organisation in addressing shipping safety and security; Parvathaneni said New Delhi is working directly with both sides on Black Sea shipping and grain export corridor safety, reiterating support for an early end to the conflict and 'enduring peace.'
items.title: India Calls for End to Black Sea Shipping Attacks at UN Security Council

visual.alt: Bar chart. MV Omorfi crew member killed 4; MV Royad Mammadov Indian nationals aboard 2.

items.summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets and briefly ordered residents of Ulleung Island to seek shelter underground after multiple Russian warplanes entered the country's air identification zone, described as the latest in a string of similar regional incidents. An air raid warning issued Tuesday for the estimated 9,000 people living on Ulleung Island—located about 130 kilometers east of the Korean Peninsula—was lifted minutes after it was initially posted on a local disaster portal. The Russian jets entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) and flew near the island, prompting South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff to deploy its fighter jets in response. In a statement, the JCS said 'The aircraft left following our military measures,' adding that there was no violation of South Korean airspace; it noted that the KADIZ is not territorial airspace but an area where aircraft are expected to identify themselves as they approach. Jang Do-young, a Joint Chiefs spokesperson, told a briefing that the Russian military aircraft had approached Ulleung Island 'to the point where it was just short of entering our airspace,' and said South Korea issued the alert preemptively given how quickly military aircraft travel; he added that such incidents have occurred multiple times but are rare for authorities to issue warnings in response. The military declined to elaborate on how close the jets flew before departing. South Korea plans to summon Russia's military attache to protest the flights, according to the Defense Ministry.
items.title: South Korea Scrambles Jets After Russian Warplanes Enter Air Zone

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) issued an advisory cautioning investors about the risks of relying on grey market premiums (GMP) to gauge initial public offering prices. Sebi explained that GMP transactions occur before a stock's formal listing, take place outside the exchange framework, are not subject to regulatory oversight, and carry neither settlement guarantees nor investor protection. The regulator also stated that these transactions do not follow any formal price discovery process. In its advisory, Sebi said that publishing such pre-listing premium figures could be detrimental to investors' interests and contrary to transparency and accountability principles in the securities market. Consequently, the regulator called for discontinuing the publication of grey market premium figures through any mode or platform across the securities market.
items.title: Sebi Warns Against Relying on Grey Market Premium as IPO Price Indicator

items.summary: Cameron Munster said he declined Melbourne Storm's latest contract offer, describing it as "disappointing." His teammate Harry Grant met with the Gold Coast last week, and Stefano Utoikamanu has been linked with the Sydney Roosters while remaining off contract for next season. Separately, in a final score result, the Rabbitohs lost 10-20 to the Knights.
items.title: Munster Rejects Melbourne Storm Contract Offer as 'Disappointing'

items.summary: On Monday, Cockroach Janta Party convenor and investigative journalist Saurav Das alleged that he was stopped at the immigration counter of Delhi airport before boarding his flight to London at 1 am. In a social media post, Das said he had been invited by prestigious universities including Oxford, Cambridge, LSE (London School of Economics), and Edinburgh to deliver talks on what he called the 'cockroach movement,' which concerns youth protests in India. He stated that an 'anti-intellectual government' was afraid of him traveling to these institutions. Hours later, Cockroach Janta Party leader Ratna Singh said she too had been invited to speak at the Oxford Union but her visa had been rejected a few days earlier; she added that Das's denial raises troubling questions about freedom of expression and space for young voices in India. On Monday, party founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that someone 'in power was jealous' of Das receiving an invitation from the University of Oxford. The Cockroach Janta Party political campaign had named Das as its chief spokesperson on June 3, days ahead of a protest demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, then Union education minister, over alleged irregularities in conducting competitive examinations; Pradhan resigned on July 25 after the protest spread to other parts of the country following a police crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi. Das was a key leader of those protests and held discussions with the Union government along with another campaign spokesperson, Ashutosh Ranka. On October 13, Das and Ranka were detained for trespassing on Jantar Mantar and waving the national flag amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in revising the voter roll; they had 'sneaked into' Jantar Mantar to oppose authorities' decision to denotify the area as a designated protest site. They were arrested a day later and released on October 21.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party's Saurav Das Alleges Delhi Airport Stop Before UK Trip

items.summary: In May, a 14-year-old girl named Vaishnavi in the hill hamlet of Peddaporlu developed what is locally called 'chali-jwaram' (chills-fever) after exposure during a storm. Her family initially received only basic treatment at the nearest government Primary Health Centre and declined to travel, as mud roads connecting their village are frequently washed away by torrential rains. After seven days of queuing with blood samples for testing, Vaishnavi was not admitted because the district hospital in Paderu has no overnight facilities; she traveled back and forth three times on a two-wheeler before doctors urged transport to King George Hospital in Visakhapatnam, 106 kilometres away. Her mother said she would prefer taking her daughter to a guru-guniya (local faith healer) who performs animal sacrifices than sending her to the hospital. After spending over Rs 1,000 on fuel across roughly 270 kilometres and around Rs 15,000 for one day's stay at a private hospital in Paderu—while Vaishnavi's family earns about Rs 7,500 per month selling agricultural produce to contractors—she was finally diagnosed with malaria. She later recovered after three days of treatment at the district hospital.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh villages give a reality check to India's 2030 malaria elimination target

items.summary: Maxine Dillion, a 44-year-old self-employed mother of two from Mansfield in Nottinghamshire who earns £32,000 a year, pays £250 a month for five hours' work with Life Laundry after struggling to keep up with her household and personal chores. Launched in 2025 by Alicia Papachristou and Jane Forbes, both based in Wakefield, Yorkshire, the company handles tasks such as arranging insurance, sending school emails, managing online subscriptions, booking handymen, and posting clothing returns on Vinted; much of the work is done remotely, with a monthly visit to Mansfield for jobs requiring physical presence. Life Laundry currently has 25 customers. Amanda Sims Nichols, a business consultant in Austin, Texas who has three children with her attorney husband, pays $2,250 (£1,750) a month for 25 hours of help from Queen of To Do after moving house away from her family support network; she relishes offloading chores such as the weekly food shop and clothes washing. Founded by Kate Ginsberg in 2011, Queen of To Do now has more than 50 active users. Both companies report growing demand as people's lives become increasingly frantic. Ginsberg said some tasks her team handles are very diverse, including flying from Austin to New York City to buy a Christmas gift and finding a new wedding location for a client with just three days' notice due to an incoming hurricane. Jess Baker, a UK chartered psychologist, said using a life PA takes the pressure off keeping hundreds of to-dos in one's head or on lists that might be forgotten, noting otherwise the cognitive load can lead to feelings of being overwhelmed, excess worry and exhaustion. Anna Allington sought help after her husband died; she was 47 when he passed away, and the same week she got leukaemia with a lot to sort out while very unwell. Now 51 and still suffering from cancer's effects because she cannot function executively like before, she pays £1,200 a month for 40 hours of help from Cheshire-based company Vi-Va; her personal assistant helps respond to emails, manage her diary, and make travel plans and bookings. They meet twice a week on Zoom so they can go through all her tasks. Many more women than men use these companies: Queen of To Do says just 20% of its clients are male, while only one of Life Laundry's 25 clients is a man. Forbes suggested some of that disparity reflects mothers still handling the lion's share of household admin in studies, and wondered if some men are too proud to ask for assistance.
items.title: Life admin companies grow as busy parents pay to offload household tasks

items.summary:
The Indian Air Force is expected to take delivery of its first locally manufactured C295 transport aircraft, built jointly by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) and Airbus, with officials reporting the aircraft is undergoing final flight trials and certification as TASL and Airbus target year-end delivery. The plane will join one of the IAF's two existing C295 squadrons based in Agra and Vadodara.

The programme traces to a September 2021 defence ministry contract with Airbus worth ₹21,935 crore for 56 planes aimed at boosting self-reliance in India's defence manufacturing sector. Of the total order, Airbus has delivered 16 aircraft to the IAF in flyaway condition from Spain while the remaining units are being assembled in India; of those remaining, delivery of the first was earlier scheduled for September-end but then-IAF chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh noted in October that minor issues were being resolved. The overall production and delivery programme remains on schedule, with officials stating the remaining 39 aircraft will be delivered by August 2031.

Atmanirbharta (self-reliance) is a key priority for current IAF chief Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who took over as Chief of the Air Staff on October 31 and outlined his vision using the acronym "VAYU"—V for vigilance and readiness, A for atmanirbharta, Y for yukti (ingenuity), and U for unity of effort. The IAF is expected to begin raising its third C295 squadron next year.

The aircraft will enhance logistics capabilities in forward areas including those near the contested border with China and replace the ageing Avro transport fleet that entered service in the early 1960s. Under the programme, India manufactures more than 13,000 parts and 4,600 sub-assemblies along with all major component assemblies, while Airbus supplies equipment such as engines, landing gear, and avionics; the tactical airlifter is powered by two Pratt & Whitney PW127G turboprop engines. The aircraft can carry up to nine tonnes of payload or 71 personnel or 45 paratroopers at a maximum speed of 480 kmph, operates from short or unprepared airstrips, and has a rear ramp for paradropping troops and cargo.
items.title: IAF to Receive First India-Made C295 Transport Aircraft by December 31

items.summary:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast isolated heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds across parts of South Peninsular India this week, attributing the activity to easterly waves over the Bay of Bengal and off the Kerala-Karnataka coast. Under troughs in these easterlies, IMD says isolated heavy rainfall is very likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal from 23 to 27 November, and over Kerala and Mahe from 24 to 27 November. Fairly widespread to widespread showers are expected across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry from 24 to 26 November; Kerala and Mahe from 24 to 27 November; and Lakshadweep from 25 to 28 November. The agency has also issued warnings for thunderstorms, lightning, and squally weather across the southern peninsula.

While West and Central India are expected to see largely dry weather during the week, IMD reports that minimum temperatures will fall gradually by 3–5°C over Central India until 26 November, by 3–4°C over East India until 27 November, and by 2–3°C over Northwest India until 28 November. Dense morning fog is very likely in isolated pockets of Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura through 25 November, with dense fog also expected over Assam and Meghalaya on 24 and 25 November.

The Met Department cautioned that reduced visibility from the fog could disrupt airport, highway, and railway operations while posing respiratory and eye-irritation risks. In Delhi-NCR, IMD forecasts mainly clear skies with mist or shallow fog during morning hours through 26 November, moderate fog likely in a few pockets on 25 and 26 November.

For the national capital specifically, IMD says Tuesday (November 24) will feature mainly clear skies with mist or shallow fog in some places during mornings. Daytime maximum temperatures are forecast to hover between 24°C and 26°C—remaining below normal by up to 1.6°C–3.0°C at most places—while minimum temperatures will settle near normal in the 10°C to 12°C range.
items.title: IMD Issues Heavy Rain Alert for Tamil Nadu and Kerala Through November 27

items.summary: Tension and uncertainty prevailed around the Karthigai Deepam lighting at the Tirupparankundram hill shrine in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita limited public assembly and restricted hilltop access. The Supreme Court allowed a restricted one-time lighting of the lamp by authorised officials at 6 PM, barring public access and processions. Following a report identifying the Deepathoon as a British-era survey stone, the state government filed a review petition. Approximately 5,600 police personnel were deployed to manage the situation, while political parties debated the matter and Hindu groups urged adherence to court orders.
items.title: Tension Rises at Tirupparankundram Hill Shrine During Karthigai Deepam Lighting

items.summary: Bihar unit chief of the AIMIM party, Akhtarul Iman, sparked a political controversy with remarks about Muslim bridal traditions. He criticized what he described as the lack of proper veiling during wedding receptions, comparing uncovered brides to courtesans and citing Sharia law's mandate for modesty. His comments were condemned by opposition leaders as sexist and derogatory toward women's dignity. Critics urged party leader Asaduddin Owaisi to respond to the controversy, raising concerns about attitudes toward women's rights and personal freedom.
items.title: AIMIM MLA Akhtarul Iman Draws Criticism Over Comments on Muslim Bridal Practices

items.summary:
On Monday (24 November 2026), UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed delivered remarks in New York on behalf of Secretary-General Antonio Guterres at a special meeting marking the International Day of Solidarity. She said Palestinians in the Gaza Strip are not receiving the safety, assistance or recovery they need despite a ceasefire, describing the devastation as "staggering" with tens of thousands killed and homes, schools and hospitals reduced to rubble while another winter settles in. Mohammed stated there is "no time to waste," "no excuse for inaction," and "no place for impunity," adding that nothing can justify collective punishment against Palestinians and that solidarity must mean acting to end suffering rather than merely bearing witness.

On the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, she said settler violence, demolitions, evictions, land seizures and displacement are driving Palestinian families from their homes at a scale not seen in generations. She warned that Israeli settlement expansion, including efforts to advance the E1 plan, threatens the viability of the two-state solution and called for these activities to stop immediately.

Mohammed also said humanitarian workers must never be targeted and aid must never be obstructed, diverted or used as a bargaining chip. She urged member states to provide political and financial support to UNRWA so it can fulfill its mandate. On recovery, she said rebuilding must be led by Palestinians, go beyond infrastructure reconstruction, and cannot substitute for a political solution; citing a joint UN and World Bank assessment that found the conflict has undone 77 years of human development in Gaza. She concluded that there can be no peace in the Middle East without realizing Palestinian self-determination, calling the two-state solution "the only viable path forward."
items.title: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed Calls for Action on Gaza as Suffering Continues

items.summary: The Trump administration added Megaspeed—the company at the center of the Nvidia scandal—to the Commerce Department's entity list on Monday afternoon, plans first reported by Semafor. The Singapore-based company was placed on the blacklist so that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. According to a filing from Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security posted to the Federal Register Monday afternoon, seven total entities were added to the list from Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including various affiliates such as MSFusion, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, and Swiftdata. The filing states that these additions are being made because of "the significant risk of these entities being or becoming involved in the diversion of advanced computing commodities to unauthorized end uses or end users," noting that licenses will be reviewed under a presumption of denial. Technology exports already en route to the targeted companies would still be allowed to go through, per the filing. The addition comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO after President Donald Trump implored them to do so; Huang had resigned less than two weeks earlier amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy who was an executive at Megaspeed. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has faced pressure from others inside the administration—and bipartisan lawmakers—to place Megaspeed on the entity list and explain his decisions around Nvidia, Megaspeed, and chip export controls; tensions became public after news broke of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier this month that his agency along with the Pentagon, State Department, and US Trade Representative had backed putting Megaspeed on the entity list "for months" but that "Commerce holds the pen." BIS spokesman Thomas Wackman told Semafor that placing Megaspeed on the Entity List makes it unlawful to export any US-origin goods, software, or technology to the company, including advanced semiconductor chips even if produced outside the United States. The Justice Department is separately investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.
items.title: Commerce Adds Megaspeed to Trade Blacklist Amid Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: At a November 24, 2026 UN Security Council briefing in Istanbul, Russia and Ukraine traded accusations over escalating attacks on Black Sea shipping and energy infrastructure. Moscow's representative accused Ukrainian forces of targeting more than 200 commercial vessels across the Black, Azov, Caspian, Baltic and Mediterranean seas since July, killing or wounding 12 seafarers, while defending its campaign as limited to military-logistical targets and dismissing Western calls for a truce. Russia's envoy also ruled out reviving a grain deal, calling any new agreement 'a scheme of Ukrainian food in exchange for Western weapons,' noting that under the previous arrangement only 3% of exported grain reached countries in need while up to 70% entered EU and Western markets; he said Russia supplies food to 160 countries. Ukraine's representative accused Russia of targeting civilian power grids since mid-July, damaging virtually every power plant alongside more than 800 units of energy equipment, with November barrages shutting down three thermal plants and plunging more than 850,000 people into darkness; he also cited the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant's 28th off-site power loss. On maritime security, Kyiv reported 89 attacks on civilian vessels between June and August, up from 25 in all of 2025, while accusing Russia of looting grain through a 'shadow grain fleet.' The Ukraine Energy Support Fund raised more than €2.4 billion ($2.6 billion) from 41 donors as Kyiv prioritized air defense for winter. US representative urged both sides to immediately halt strikes on energy grids, civilian ports, food distribution sites and commercial shipping, highlighting progress with four pillars aimed at building toward a lasting peace.
items.title: Russia and Ukraine Clash at UN Over Black Sea Shipping and Energy Strikes

items.summary: The Airline Pilots' Association of India (ALPA India) has urged the Civil Aviation Ministry to examine whether SpiceJet's financial difficulties are creating risks for flight safety. In a letter dated November 17, signed by Captain Sam Thomas, President and IFALPA Director of ALPA India, the association raised concerns over delayed salary payments to pilots and cabin crew, pending maintenance organisation and spare-parts supplier payments, and employee pressure during repeated flight disruptions. ALPA warned that financial uncertainty and stress from unpaid salaries could affect the alertness, concentration and decision-making of employees responsible for passenger safety, arguing aviation professionals should not perform safety-critical duties while struggling with basic financial commitments. The association also highlighted difficulties faced by pilots, cabin crew and ground staff during delays, cancellations and other operational disruptions, noting frontline employees increasingly face passenger frustration despite having little control over management decisions causing such disruptions. ALPA flagged the possible impact of financial constraints on aircraft maintenance, warning that payment delays to maintenance organisations, spare-parts suppliers and essential service providers could result in grounded aircraft and further operational disruptions while increasing workload pressure on engineering personnel. The association questioned what it described as the DGCA's apparent double standards in enforcing employment-related regulations, pointing out that the regulator strictly applies Civil Aviation Requirements concerning notice periods and No Objection Certificates when pilots want to leave an airline, yet reportedly tells employees the regulator cannot intervene in contractual matters when airlines delay or fail to pay salaries. ALPA argued that if notice periods are justified for flight safety, persistent non-payment of salaries must equally be recognised as a flight safety concern. The association has asked the Civil Aviation Ministry and DGCA to urgently examine the safety implications of financial distress at SpiceJet and other similarly affected airlines, with demands including closer monitoring of aircraft maintenance resources and payments, timely salary payment to pilots and cabin crew, and a faster release and NOC process when employers have demonstrably failed contractual obligations. The letter was marked to the Director General of Civil Aviation and the Prime Minister's Office. These concerns come amid continuing operational difficulties at SpiceJet, with flight disruptions and passenger complaints adding to questions about the airline's financial and operational position.
items.title: ALPA Warns SpiceJet Financial Troubles Raise Flight Safety Concerns

items.summary: Demonstrators gathered in Brussels carrying placards warning that 'Rent is eating into our wages' and 'The rich earn more, the workers pay more,' to oppose approximately €10 billion in proposed spending cuts. The planned savings would affect social security, employment support, and family assistance while burdening low-income earners already strained by high energy costs, inflation, and shrinking purchasing power. Clashes broke out between protesters and riot police as a car burned amid plumes of smoke; officers responded with tear gas, water cannons, and charges, making arrests in the process. The street protests coincided with Prime Minister Bart De Wever's meeting with King Philippe to update him on strained negotiations over Belgium's 2027 budget. Having set a year-end deadline for coalition partners to approve the cuts and warned that the government could collapse if talks fail, De Wever now faces mounting resistance both in parliament and on the streets as he attempts to balance fiscal discipline against demands to protect living standards.
items.title: Belgian Workers March Against Spending Cuts Amid Rising Living Costs

items.summary: Papua New Guinea's parliament is voting to ratify the result of a 2019 referendum in which almost 98% of Bougainvillean voters chose independence. A 'yes' vote would not immediately create an independent nation but would set legal machinery in motion toward self-determination, while a 'no' or deferred vote would trigger further consultations and protective measures.
items.title: PNG Parliament Votes on Ratifying Bougainville Independence

items.summary: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced during a Monday media briefing that India's first bullet train is expected to begin trial runs in May 2027 on the 50-km Surat-Bilimora stretch of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor. He said electrification work on the section had been completed, while signalling-related work was targeted for completion by January 2027.
items.title: India's First Bullet Train to Begin Trials in May 2027, Railway Minister Announces

items.summary: A Dutch court barred European sales of a BYD vehicle over its resemblance to Jaguar Land Rover's Defender, causing BYD shares to slide Monday and marking a setback for the Chinese automaker's Europe expansion plans. The affected model is not yet on sale in the EU, and Reuters noted it was rare for European automakers to sue over design rights infringement. This case reflects broader efforts by the EU to protect its car industry from Chinese competitors amid aggressive overseas expansion; Chinese brands captured a record 14.5% of Europe's market in September. However, while European automakers may welcome the ruling, the vehicle—nicknamed the 'Temu Range Rover'—has been the UK's best-selling car for months.
items.title: Dutch Court Bars BYD Vehicle Over Range Rover Resemblance

items.summary: Ohio regulators approved construction of an 800-megawatt natural gas plant to power a data center complex in Ashville, Ohio, even though local voters overwhelmingly rejected the project. The permit approval is not unique nationally—energy-hungry developers are building similar gas-fired generation across the U.S.—but critics say it highlights Ohio's leniency toward fossil-fuel projects versus its strict restrictions on solar and wind farms that often face denial due to local opposition.
items.title: Ohio Approves Gas Plant for Data Centers Despite Local Voter Rejection

items.summary: According to findings published in The Innovation, mangrove cover in China more than doubled between 1998 and 2020, while the number of bird species recorded in those areas rose from 148 to 397. This recovery follows decades of steep decline: China lost nearly 70% of its mangroves between 1950 and 1990. Since then, the government has set aside mangrove reserves and restored degraded areas, including former aquaculture ponds, according to researchers who also attribute part of the growth to rising temperatures and increased rainfall favoring mangrove expansion.
items.title: China's Mangrove Cover Doubled and Bird Species Rose From 148 to 397

visual.alt: Bar chart. Before recovery (baseline) 148; After recovery (2020) 397.

items.summary: Morocco staged a comeback from two goals down to secure a late draw against China, keeping their hopes of advancing alive ahead of a decisive match with Group H leaders Spain. Coach Ahmed Kantari praised his players' resilience and focus throughout the game, stating that they deserved the result despite conceding early. A Moroccan player also credited the supporters for helping the team perform well. Morocco now require at least a draw against Spain to guarantee their place in the round of 32.
items.title: Crucial Draw Sets Up Decisive Morocco–Spain Showdown

items.summary: The Guardian interviewed experts across aviation, banking, and national security fields about how AI and other threats are jeopardizing critical infrastructure following a series of recent system disruptions. In the weeks leading up to these interviews, there had been grounded flights, crashing bank websites, Microsoft Outlook outages halting business operations, and hacked sites for Zoom, Ikea, and PokerStars, prompting public speculation about coordinated cyber-attacks by Iranian hackers or autonomous AI agents targeting air traffic control and banking systems.
items.title: Experts Assess Risks to Critical Infrastructure After Recent Mass Outages

items.summary: The COP31 climate conference in Turkey became the longest UN climate talks in history over the weekend, but negotiations failed to produce a deal after the European Union and several countries rejected a final proposal due to its omission of fossil fuels. The breakdown has fueled growing frustration across Europe and raised questions about whether the international climate diplomacy process can still deliver meaningful results or has reached a breaking point. Euronews' Felicia Pochhammer interviewed Chiara Martinelli, director of Climate Action Network, on Europe Tonight to examine what went wrong at the talks in Turkey and what the failed negotiations mean for Europe and the future of global climate action.
items.title: COP31 Talks Fail as EU Rejects Deal Over Fossil Fuel Omission

items.summary: On Monday, Ukraine claimed it was responsible for strikes on two Russian vessels off the coast of Libya, including an attack that sank a modern warship. The attacks occurred Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi and represent the latest spillover from Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This comes as Ukraine has increased its daring long-range strikes against targets far from the frontlines in retaliation for Moscow's deadly invasion.
items.title: Ukraine Claims It Sank Russian Warship Off Libya

items.summary: An essay published in The Humanist Review of AI argues that artificial intelligence generates consumer welfare gains through increased product customization and variety, which are not captured by standard quality-based adjustments to gross domestic product. According to the author, new or newly available customized products typically produce larger welfare gains than established products: because such products were previously unavailable—effectively carrying an infinite price for consumers—they become accessible at normal prices when introduced, representing a substantial effective price decline that can be especially large if the consumer values the product highly. The essay notes that comparable gains are harder to achieve by simply purchasing more of an existing product already available over time.
items.title: Essay Argues AI's Product Customization Gains Are Missed by GDP

items.summary: Disguised test vehicles of Hyundai's third-generation Kona have been spotted in the US, Europe, and South Korea over recent months. The new model appears to skip the typical mid-cycle refresh that followed the 2023 second-generation launch, instead receiving a complete redesign with a higher stance and more commanding SUV-like shape similar to the Santa Fe, Palisade, and Tucson. Two versions have been captured: a standard Kona and a rugged XRT variant. For the first time, HealerTV spotted the new Kona N Line in Korea on a car carrier; because it is covered and an early-stage prototype, only exclusive wheels and added lower side skirts are clearly visible, though other N Line design elements such as more aggressive front and rear bumpers are expected. The sighting suggests Hyundai will keep the N Line trim in the third-gen lineup. The new Kona is expected to debut in 2027 as a 2028 model year and be available in gas, hybrid, and fully electric powertrains like the current generation; earlier this month a prototype believed to be the EV version was captured in Korea. Hyundai skipped the 2026 Kona Electric in the US but said it would return for the 2027 model year when the third-generation model arrives.
items.title: Hyundai Spotted Testing New Third-Generation Kona N Line Prototype

items.summary: At the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Doha, Qatar, Mali's under-17 team came from behind to defeat Belgium 2-1. Belgium took an early lead with a goal in the 13th minute, but Djiguo Koita equalized five minutes later at the 18-minute mark. Yaya Niang then scored the winning goal in the second half, completing the comeback for Mali's Young Eagles.
items.title: Mali Beat Belgium 2-1 to Strengthen Under-17 World Cup Qualification Hopes

items.summary:
In South Africa's Limpopo province, residents are still recovering from the January floods that exposed weaknesses in infrastructure and prompted concerns about preparedness for the upcoming rainy season. The January flooding damaged roads, bridges, and water systems across the region, leaving communities to contend with ongoing damage months later while looking ahead uncertainly toward future rains.

In Boelang village, located about 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) southwest of Ba-Phalaborwa in Limpopo's Mopani district, residents had gone without municipal water for almost three months after two main pipelines crossing the Selati River were washed away and a pump station failed. Repairs completed in March restored their water supply, but resident Shanine noted that water pressure remained unreliable with water sometimes flowing slowly. She expressed uncertainty about whether the repaired infrastructure could withstand another flood, pointing out that the community's water system sits directly in the Selati River.

The January floods left a trail of destruction across Limpopo, disrupting learners from attending school and severely damaging water infrastructure. In Ba-Phalaborwa town, residents were placed on a water-shedding schedule as flooding washed away the infrastructure supplying their water supply. Trevor van Rooyen, vice chairperson of the Let's Change Ba-Phalaborwa Community Forum, told Mongabay that he did not believe the government was adequately prepared for further flooding, noting that while damaged roads were patched and bridges destroyed are still under construction.

The damage extended beyond Ba-Phalaborwa. About 170 km away in Tshikunda village under Thulamela municipality, part of a road was washed away in January; by mid-November when Mongabay visited, motorists had created an alternative route through the damaged section that was too narrow for two vehicles to pass simultaneously. Residents of Tshikunda and nearby Tshitereke village are calling on the Limpopo Department of Public Works to urgently repair the Tshikunda bypass road D3681, which links their villages to local schools and Donald Fraser Hospital.

Emmanuel Mongwe, spokesperson for the Limpopo Department of Public Works, Roads and Infrastructure, said work was being finalized on the Tshikunda bypass road as an interim measure while appointing a contractor, with that process expected to be completed by end of November after which construction would resume. Regarding the damaged Selati River bridge, Mongwe said it falls under South African National Roads Agency (SANRAL) responsibility and the department is receiving updates on repair work.

Tsakani Baloyi, director of communications for the Limpopo Department of Cooperative Governance, Human Settlements and Traditional Affairs, told Mongabay that the department had purchased temporary residential units worth 53 million rand ($3 million) to house residents whose homes may be destroyed by rains expected in January 2027. The units were distributed across the province's five districts: Vhembe, Capricorn, Mopani, Waterberg and Sekhukhune, with blankets also available for distribution.

Hope Magidimisha, a national planning commissioner in the Office of the Presidency, said disaster preparedness must begin long before heavy rains arrive. She emphasized identifying vulnerable communities and infrastructure—settlements near rivers, streams and flood lines as well as roads, bridges, schools and other public facilities—and called for greater attention to drainage systems including regular inspections and maintenance before the rainy season.

Magidimisha stressed that early-warning systems are a priority: weather warnings must reach communities in time and in languages people understand so they know what to do when issued. She said an early warning is only useful if it leads to early action, noting it is not enough for the South African Weather Service to issue warnings.

Magidimisha also called for the government to consider long-term solutions including relocation where settlements are situated in dangerous locations, acknowledging this is difficult because people have homes, livelihoods and community connections. She said preparedness should be assessed regularly—identifying vulnerable areas, clearing drainage systems, preparing evacuation plans, ensuring emergency teams are ready and repairing damaged roads and bridges—and that the measure of success should be whether communities are safer rather than money spent or meetings held.

She advised residents to know whether they live in flood-prone areas, where to go during an emergency and whom to contact when their lives or property are threatened, with community leaders involved in preparedness planning particularly for older people, children and people with disabilities. Magidimisha said effective flood preparedness depends on disaster management structures, infrastructure departments, municipalities and communities working together.
items.title: Limpopo Residents Worry About Next Flood After January Damage

items.summary: Analysts at Boston Consulting Group (BCG) said in a September analysis that if quantum-enabled advances in materials, chemistry, and industrial processes reach commercial scale, implications could extend far beyond emissions savings—potentially transforming electricity generation and storage, food production, and carbon removal. BCG experts noted quantum computers are currently better than classical computing and AI at simulating how molecules and materials behave, which could help discover new materials, compounds, battery chemistries, or catalysts for cleaner energy in sectors where renewables cannot reduce the carbon footprint—such as steel-making, cement, aluminum, chemicals, shipping, and aviation. BCG added that breakthrough battery chemistries discovered with quantum modeling could accelerate electrification rates globally by potentially making electricity cheaper and more accessible, but major quantum-driven changes and significant emissions reductions could be years away depending on scaling.
items.title: Quantum Computing Could Accelerate the Energy Transition

items.summary: Noelia Ordieres Buarfa-Mohamed, a 41-year-old climber from Llanes who was recovering from a broken right leg sustained training on an indoor climbing wall — two operations, six months in a wheelchair, and sixteen screws later — climbed to the summit of Lenin Peak at the Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border. She reached the Edelweiss meadow where eight Soviet climbers are buried there but found no signage, marked trail, or plaque; she said their names aloud out loud and decided to tell their story.
items.title: Climber retraces the fatal descent of the first all-female team to Lenin Peak

items.summary: The State Bank of India (SBI) has advised the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to consider a modest 25 basis points rate hike in its December monetary policy rather than a jumbo 50 bps increase, warning that an aggressive move could trigger capital outflows, currency instability, and concerns over economic growth. The report emphasized the need for financial stability amid growing global market uncertainty as it prepared ahead of the RBI Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting scheduled for December 2–4, with the policy decision to be announced on December 4.
items.title: SBI Advises RBI on Cautious 25 bps Hike Amid Calls for Jumbo Rate Cut

items.summary:
South Indian Bank (SIB) disclosed that the Reserve Bank of India has approved SBI Mutual Fund's acquisition of up to 9.99 per cent of the bank's paid-up share capital or voting rights, as reported in a regulatory filing published on November 24, 2026. The approval is conditional on compliance with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; RBI directions governing commercial banks' acquisition and holding of shares or voting rights; the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999; Securities and Exchange Board of India regulations; and any other applicable statutes, regulations, and guidelines.

As at September-end 2026, public shareholding in South Indian Bank stood at 100 per cent. Mutual funds collectively held a 15.13 per cent stake in the Thrissur (Kerala)-headquartered private sector bank, distributed across Kotak Mahindra Trustee Co Ltd's A/C Kotak Multicap Fund (6.05 per cent), Bandhan Small Cap Fund (4.69 per cent), and SBI Banking & Financial Services Fund (2.90 per cent).
items.title: RBI Approves SBI Mutual Fund to Acquire Up to 9.99% of South Indian Bank

items.summary: Following NVIDIA's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO, Krishnamoorthi posted on X urging House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast to hold a full public hearing with Huang. He argued that Congress and the American public deserve transparency about what Chinese intelligence may have obtained from Huang and whether advanced American AI technology was compromised, insisting such questions be answered publicly rather than behind closed doors. His demand comes amid growing scrutiny of NVIDIA over allegations concerning possible Chinese intelligence links and the diversion of advanced American semiconductor products for military applications in China. Krishnamoorthi stated that Trump Administration's rush to reinstate Huang underscores the need for Congress to act, accusing it of putting its own financial interests before national security, and pledged Democratic investigations into any wrongdoing by the administration, Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out national security for financial gain, while also pursuing bipartisan policies to stop advanced technology flowing to China. Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance welcomed Huang's return on X with a post reading 'Welcome back Jensen.' According to a Financial Times report, disclosures of Trump's investment portfolio through the end of September indicated his NVIDIA holdings had potentially increased in value by approximately USD 15 million. Trump subsequently acknowledged speaking to NVIDIA's board regarding Huang's position and told CNBC he did not use the word 'prosecuted' but assured the company that 'he's absolutely fine,' adding that if he thought Huang did something wrong, he would not recommend his reinstatement. US lawmakers maintained that NVIDIA's internal investigation and the board's decision do not resolve broader national security concerns; House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI), House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford (R-AR), and House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast (R-FL) issued a joint statement saying the company's internal review does not erase the threats that must be addressed, noting Huang and Tim Teter confirmed they will appear for transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as planned. NVIDIA announced Monday that Huang had been reinstated with immediate effect as President and CEO and Board member; according to a statement from NVIDIA's Board of Directors, the unanimous decision followed discussions and meetings with Huang, who apologized to employees upon returning to headquarters in Santa Clara, California, saying 'I've made some very terrible mistakes.'
items.title: Krishnamoorthi Urges Public Hearing With Nvidia's Jensen Huang Amid National Security Scrutiny

items.summary:
President Donald Trump intervened to restore Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, demonstrating how he can wield influence despite Republicans losing control of Congress. After the Nvidia board ruled out restoring Huang following revelations about his relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and other women, Trump made a forceful case for Huang's return at a Friday press conference, then dispatched administration members over the weekend to convince the board to reverse its position in an announcement shortly before Monday's market open. Trump celebrated on CNBC, calling Huang a 'national treasure' and stating there was no national security problem after research.

The stock market soared following the reversal, while some Members of Congress criticized the move. Senate Majority Leader John Thune warned that allowing China to obtain America's most advanced chips creates a significant national security vulnerability and promised strong export control measures. Former Speaker Newt Gingrich called Huang's reinstatement 'profoundly wrong' and urged Congress to investigate it as a national security issue.

Trump's intervention extended his pattern of inserting himself into major corporate decisions, including pushing deals involving Intel and US Steel. After blocking Nippon Steel's bid for US Steel in a $14.9 billion acquisition, the Japanese company agreed to give Trump unusual power over the company's future, including authority to name a board member and final say on idling plants, production cuts, and moving jobs overseas. The administration also negotiated a 10 per cent stake in Intel by converting government grants into equity, called for Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan's resignation before announcing the deal making the US government the biggest shareholder.

Trump's team additionally struck an agreement allowing Nvidia to sell its H20 chips to China in exchange for receiving 15 per cent of those sales, and reached a deal with MP Materials that would make the Pentagon the largest shareholder in the rare earth magnet producer. Democrats vowed to investigate once they take control of Congress in January, with Huang scheduled to testify at a hearing next week.
items.title: Trump Intervenes to Restore Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO Amid Lame-Duck Phase

visual.alt: Bar chart. Intel stake (grants converted) 10 %; Nvidia H20 chip sales to China 15 %.

items.summary: President Trump publicly praised the reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, telling The New York Times that Huang had 'worked it out' with his wife Lori Huang. Speaking in an interview published Monday after Nvidia's board voted to reinstate Huang as chief executive, Trump said, 'He's got a very, very, very good wife, and they've worked it out,' adding that 'She's a fantastic woman.' He was referring to Lori Huang, a major Nvidia shareholder who has not spoken publicly since reports emerged about her husband's close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman unrelated to him. Trump also backed the board's decision in writing, stating on social media that 'The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,' and arguing that 'The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.' He said he had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk, noting that the attorney general confirmed the government did not have evidence of unlawful conduct by Huang. Trump described himself as having 'gotten to know Jensen,' calling him 'a Great Patriot and National Treasure,' while also urging Nvidia to continue its internal investigation into whether the company complied with U.S. export controls so it could fulfill what he called its 'Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security.' He had earlier urged the board on Truth Social that bringing Huang back would be 'the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.,' telling CNBC that he 'convinced them' and 'made the deal.' Separately, reports estimated a possible divorce settlement exceeding $60 billion — with one estimate reaching $81.1 billion based on Huang's reported net worth at the time under California community property laws assuming an equal division of marital assets; however, neither Jensen nor Lori Huang had announced a divorce, and these figures were hypothetical estimates rather than confirmed payments. The couple have been married since 1985 and have two children.
items.title: Trump Praises Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia and Comments on His Marriage

items.summary: Shares in Nvidia jumped 30% on Monday after the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang, who had resigned less than two weeks earlier over an alleged Chinese spy scandal and an affair with an employee. The news helped spark a recovery across markets following a technology-led rout last week during which major indices fell between seven and 10%. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, described Huang as the 'AI comeback kid' but cautioned that volatility was not over because Nvidia remained under scrutiny from investigators including the FBI and Capitol Hill. Kathleen Brooks of XTB noted that Nvidia's directors could see no future for the company without him. US President Donald Trump, who pressed for Huang's reinstatement, said on social media that the government had 'no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security' and praised the board's decision.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Surge After Jensen Huang's Reinstatement Lifts Markets

visual.alt: Bar chart. Nvidia shares 30 %; Nasdaq (US) 7 %; S&P 500 (US) 5 %; Dow Jones (US) 2.6 %; Frankfurt (Europe) 2.2 %; London / Paris (Europe) 1.5 %.

items.summary: A joint investigation by German newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung and public broadcasters NDR and WDR reports that Western intelligence agencies, including the Bundeswehr and Germany's Federal Intelligence Service (BND), assess Moscow intends to launch a satellite equipped with nuclear explosives as early as this year. The findings were shared among several NATO countries in recent days, and Bundeswehr experts reportedly briefed senior German politicians, including Defence Minister Boris Pistorius of the SPD. A spokesperson for Germany's Federal Ministry of Defence cited secrecy and confidentiality while stating that officials are continuously monitoring developments in space and other states' activities. Russian state news agency TASS reported that Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev asserted that actions by Ukraine and NATO have created circumstances under which Moscow weighs potential use of nuclear weapons, though he emphasized restraint and proportionality before any strike. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the reports shocking but not new, while NATO Chief Mark Rutte said the alliance is assessing its deterrence and defence capabilities across land, sea, air and space. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reiterated that NATO membership remains Ukraine's clearest security guarantee. During historic trilateral talks with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Putin echoed shared global stewardship while Trump said the three largest nuclear powers are positioned to discuss reducing arsenals; following the summit, the countries adopted a joint Declaration towards Peace reaffirming that a nuclear war cannot be won or fought.
items.title: German Intelligence Warns Russia May Place Nuclear Weapon in Space by Year-End

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee meets from 2 to 4 December, with the repo rate unchanged at 5.50% after a 0.25 percentage point increase in October that shifted its stance to 'calibrated tightening.' Governor Sanjay Malhotra said rate cuts were 'off the table in the near term,' though the committee's next decision remains unknown. Retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, per the statistics ministry's 12 November release—above RBI's 6% upper tolerance band—with food inflation at 8.94%. In its October projection, RBI forecast full-year 2026-27 inflation at 5.2%. Banks pass repo changes to floating-rate loans: SBI raised home loan rates by 0.25 percentage points from 15 October (now ranging 7.50% to 8.80%), and HDFC Bank raised lending rates by up to 0.15 percentage points, per Business Today. Worked examples assume an 8.25% home loan with 20 years remaining: a ₹30 lakh loan's EMI rises from ₹25,562 to ₹26,035 (+₹473/month), a ₹50 lakh loan from ₹42,603 to ₹43,391 (+₹788/month), and a ₹1 crore loan by ₹1,576/month (to ₹86,782). For a borrower at 8% before October, two 0.25-point rises would raise a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan from ₹41,822 to ₹43,391 (+₹1,569/month) and a ₹1 crore loan by ₹3,138/month combined. If RBI holds the rate in December, the October hike stays in place; borrowers should check their bank's new external benchmark rate (EBLR), its effective date, and whether their loan resets immediately or on a fixed quarterly date. Banks may raise EMIs or extend tenure: for a ₹50 lakh loan rising from 8.25% to 8.50%, holding the EMI at ₹42,603 would extend remaining tenure by roughly 12 months, raising it to ₹43,391 adds about ₹1.89 lakh in total repayments versus retaining a 20-year schedule, and extending tenure costs approximately ₹5.17 lakh more than the original schedule. These figures are worked examples, not forecasts or advice.
items.title: RBI's December MPC Meeting Approaches as Repo Rate Holds at 5.50% and Inflation Rises to 6.09%

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said he convinced Nvidia's board of directors to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, telling CNBC on Monday that he spoke directly and indirectly with them about the decision. Describing the outcome as 'very exciting news,' Trump stated plainly: 'I made the deal.' He explained his motivation by saying he feared China could otherwise approach Huang with an offer to lead Huawei or another Chinese company, given his expertise in advanced chip technology. The claims are attributed to Trump's own statements during the phone interview.
items.title: Trump Claims Credit for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia

items.summary: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index is set to expand from 30 to 50 stocks in the first major overhaul of its benchmark in 17 years. New constituents will be selected based on full market capitalisation, with additions announced December 3 and a phased inclusion beginning later that month—20 new stocks entering at half weight on December 21 before reaching full weight in June 2027. The change aims to reduce the index's reliance on banks and utilities, which account for nearly 60% of its weight, giving investors broader representation beyond those sectors.
items.title: Malaysia Expands KLCI Index to 50 Stocks, Spotlighting Tech and Power for 2027

items.summary:
Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive officer, reversing a decision made just 11 days earlier after revelations about his reported extramarital relationships. The announcement triggered a sharp rally in the company's shares, adding $952 billion to its market value in a single trading session and pushing Nvidia shares up more than 30%, which CNN described as their third-best trading day on record; the Nasdaq Composite rose 6.51%. Forbes estimated Huang's fortune at approximately $143 billion, reflecting a single-day increase of $33 billion.

The reinstatement followed an intervention by US President Donald Trump, who mobilized senior administration officials to persuade Nvidia's board to bring Huang back. According to people familiar with the matter cited by CNN, Trump had been concerned about the impact of Huang's departure on the stock market and broader US economy, concluding that restoring the CEO was necessary to stabilize investor confidence and prevent the country from losing a key figure in the global AI race. Trump personally contacted board members to vouch for Huang, whom he considers critical to America's artificial intelligence ambitions and its economic competition with China.

Vice President JD Vance led the White House pressure campaign, becoming the administration's principal emissary using his connections in Silicon Valley. The Associated Press reported that Vance stepped up his involvement over the weekend to make Trump's case to the board, and CNN reported that he coordinated directly with Huang over 72 hours, assuring the board that the government had found no evidence that the CEO committed anything illegal or threatened national security. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were also involved in the effort according to CNN.

According to news agency Reuters, US Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton played roles in determining Huang was not a security risk to the US and saw no evidence he did anything illegal or untoward related to national security. Speaking to CNBC on Monday, Trump acknowledged his role in the decision, saying "I believe my intervention was very important," adding that he had spoken to Huang on Sunday and that the executive promised to work harder following his return.

The intervention followed concerns about Huang's reported extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman US officials suspected could have links to Chinese intelligence. Another relationship reportedly involved a direct subordinate. Nvidia's board said it would complete its investigation into the national security concerns. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department is adding Megaspeed — where Alice Huang was an executive and which purchased Nvidia chips that US officials feared could reach China — to the US Entity List, restricting its access to US exports according to a notice scheduled for publication in the Federal Register.

Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next Thursday, where questions about his conduct, Nvidia's China strategy and the administration's intervention are expected to remain under scrutiny.
items.title: Trump and Vance pressure campaign leads White House to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Singapore-listed offshore, marine and energy specialist Seatrium announced on Nov 24 that it will reduce about 2% of its workforce in the Republic as part of a broader effort to streamline global operations following a consolidation of its yards and subsidiaries. As of August 2025, the company employed about 12,000 staff in Singapore and about 24,000 employees across the world.
items.title: Seatrium to Lay Off 2% of Singapore Workforce in First Restructuring Since Merger

items.summary:
A report released by SBI Research on Tuesday urged the Reserve Bank of India to prioritise financial stability in its upcoming December monetary policy meeting, recommending that a 25 basis points (bps) repo rate hike would be sufficient to address the prevailing inflation trajectory rather than an aggressive 50 bps increase. The research warned that a jumbo rate hike could trigger unintended economic consequences—including capital outflows, rupee volatility, and slower economic growth—particularly amid mounting global financial uncertainty and growing pressure on international equity markets.

The report also examined vulnerabilities in the US housing sector during November, noting that US mortgage debt has reached $13.3 trillion while consumer credit interest rates remain elevated at 11.9%, which SBI Research said is increasing household debt servicing costs and weakening housing affordability and demand. The research observed that despite homeowner equity standing at around 110% of US GDP, housing mobility remains constrained as existing borrowers are reluctant to surrender their previously secured lower mortgage rates.

Addressing investor behaviour amid growing economic uncertainty, the report highlighted a shift toward gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which recorded net inflows of $706 million during the first fortnight of November—reversing net outflows of $657 million in October. SBI Research drew parallels with previous financial crises, when it noted that precious metal prices recovered sharply while equity markets remained under pressure.

On exchange rate management, the report emphasised the importance of currency stability amid changing global financial conditions, arguing that movements beyond a certain threshold could amplify economic shocks rather than absorb them. Against this backdrop, SBI Research concluded that a measured interest rate increase would help the RBI balance inflation management, financial stability, and economic growth without intensifying existing market vulnerabilities.
items.title: SBI Research Advocates a Calibrated 25 Bps Rate Hike Ahead of the RBI's December Policy Meeting

items.summary:
President Donald Trump claimed credit for persuading Nvidia’s board to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang, telling CNBC that his administration had given the directors assurances about national security implications of the return. Speaking on the network, Trump said he was represented at a board meeting and later stated he spoke directly with the directors and convinced them to bring Huang back; when asked whether he assured them Huang would not face prosecution, he replied that he did not use the word prosecuted but provided sufficient reassurance. He defended his intervention as serving the national interest while declining to announce an investment plan or a fixed formula for intervening in corporate leadership.

Three Republican congressional committee chairmen said the reinstatement does not end their scrutiny of Nvidia’s dealings with China, issuing a joint statement that the board’s brief internal investigation and Huang’s return do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed. The lawmakers identified concerns about suspected large-scale smuggling of Nvidia products, diversion for Chinese military purposes, and contributions to China’s artificial intelligence capabilities, noting these remain subjects of inquiry rather than established findings.

The three chairmen are Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, John Moolenaar of the Select Committee on China, and Rick Crawford of the House Intelligence Committee. They said Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter had confirmed they would attend interviews previously scheduled for December 1 and December 2; those arrangements were announced November 17 as transcribed interviews with formally recorded answers.

Nvidia separately reported its board voted unanimously to restore Huang as president, chief executive, and a director effective immediately, stating that discussions satisfied directors about his candor and ability to lead. The company said input from senior US government officials gave the board confidence that his reinstatement posed no national security risk while an independent directors’ investigation continues; Nvidia launched that inquiry following reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

Nvidia also stated it would continue cooperating with government investigations, that Huang supported and will cooperate with the ongoing inquiry, and that its board has established a committee overseeing national security and export-control risks. The company is searching for a chief compliance officer.
items.title: Trump Credits Role in Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Return; Lawmakers Continue China Chip Probe

items.summary:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang returned to the company's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on Monday after its board unanimously reinstated him as president and chief executive officer. Employees greeted his return with a loud ovation following a video message he shared, in which he thanked them for giving him “a second chance” and said he intended to be a better CEO. Huang had stepped down earlier that month amid reports of alleged extramarital affairs, including two involving Nvidia employees and another with a woman allegedly tied to China; the allegations remain under scrutiny while Nvidia conducts an independent investigation into his reported relationship with Alice Huang. In announcing the reinstatement, Nvidia's board said it was satisfied with Huang's “candor” on the matter and that his return “poses no national security risk,” citing input from senior US government officials. Board chair Harvey Jones stated the company believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia and expressed confidence in working with him as he resumes leadership.

President Donald Trump claimed credit for Huang's reinstatement, telling CNBC on Monday that he had spoken with the board and “convinced them” to bring the co-founder back. Huang has been a Trump ally who previously lobbied his administration to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced H200 chips to China.

Huang's return coincided with a sharp rally in Nvidia shares and the broader US stock market. According to figures reported, Nvidia stock jumped 31.48% on Monday — its biggest one-day gain since 2003 and its third-best session on record — adding $952 billion to the company's market value in a single day. The stock climbed as much as 36.6% before paring gains, helping fuel a wider technology-led rally with the Nasdaq Composite rising 6.51% and the S&P 500 gaining 4.73%; both indexes recorded their biggest single-session gains since April 2025.

Huang's return does not end scrutiny of the company. Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott said Huang would testify before the panel on December 3, amid continuing questions around national security and Nvidia's dealings involving China.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO Amid Stock Surge
