This release improves navigation by fragment hashes for deeper integration with other Datasette plugins that update fragment hashes when the user interacts with the plugin in a way that changes state. The author built this version in order to fix some bugs with the more recent datasette-charts 0.2a0 release.
items.title: Datasette Agent Releases Version 0.7a1

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh is expanding its technology infrastructure and incentives beyond Noida as HCLTech grows its Lucknow campus, seeking to create local employment, strengthen skills, and distribute technology investment across regions. For years the state's IT story has largely been a Noida story, with that city emerging as the main hub; the government now wants to take the ecosystem into cities such as Lucknow, Kanpur, Varanasi, and Gorakhpur by expanding infrastructure, offering incentives, and building a talent pipeline. The expansion is taking shape through new Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) facilities, policy changes, and fresh investments by companies already operating in the state.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh Expands IT Infrastructure Beyond Noida

items.summary:
The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear on Wednesday renewed bail petitions filed by activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid challenging the Delhi High Court's refusal to grant them bail in a case under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. According to Press Trust of India, the pleas test prolonged UAPA detention as protected witnesses remain unexamined and a court-set deadline nears.

Imam and Khalid have been detained since 2020 after being booked on allegations that they were among the masterminds of the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots. The violence broke out during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, and the National Register of Citizens, leaving 53 people dead and more than 700 injured according to PTI.

In his petition, Imam said the charge sheet was filed on September 25, 2020. It named 18 accused while the prosecution cited more than 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses. He stated that despite spending six years and nine months as an undertrial prisoner, the prosecution had not examined a single witness.

Khalid also cited the failure to examine protected witnesses, arguing that once the one-year waiting period expires his continued imprisonment would violate Article 21 of the Constitution, which protects the right to life and personal liberty. Imam was arrested on August 25, 2020, and Khalid on September 13, 2020.

The Delhi High Court refused bail to both men on September 30, saying it was bound by "judicial discipline" and could not modify the Supreme Court's January 5 order. That order allowed the two accused to seek bail after the examination of protected witnesses or the expiry of one year, whichever came earlier.

The trial court had rejected their bail petitions for a third time on July 4, saying it had "no option but to follow" the Supreme Court's January 5 order and could neither consider the petitions nor grant relief. The high court noted that while denying bail in January, the Supreme Court described Khalid and Imam as the "ideological drivers" of the alleged conspiracy.

On September 2, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to both men; on January 5, the Supreme Court upheld that verdict but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and N V Anjaria had observed there was a case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA at first sight.

On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months' interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad. It also referred to a larger bench the issue of prolonged imprisonment of undertrial prisoners under the UAPA because of the law's strict bail conditions. Other accused including activist Khalid Saifi and former Aam Aadmi Party councillor Tahir Hussain were also booked for their alleged involvement in the case, which is being investigated by the Delhi Police Special Cell.

According to the Supreme Court's cause list, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana is likely to hear the petitions. The Supreme Court will now consider Imam's and Khalid's renewed requests for bail based on the prosecution's failure to examine protected witnesses and the approaching expiry of the one-year period fixed by the court.
items.title: Supreme Court to Hear Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid Bail Pleas

items.summary:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are expected to announce their alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly elections on Tuesday at a joint press conference scheduled for 1pm at BJP headquarters in New Delhi, according to news agency ANI. Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP chief Nitin Nambiar, and SAD supremo Sukhbir Singh Badal will attend the event.

The alliance revives ties between the two parties that ended their decades-old partnership in 2020 after the Akali Dal walked out of the National Democratic Alliance over the now-repealed farm laws. Under their previous arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats while the SAD fought the remaining constituencies.

BJP sources indicated earlier that the party would contest a substantially higher number of seats than under the prior arrangement as it seeks to expand its political footprint in the state. The BJP has stepped up outreach with an aggressive campaign against drug addiction and opposition to religious conversions by missionaries among key planks, and has inducted leaders from other parties.

The alliance comes amid improved electoral performance for the BJP following its 2024 Lok Sabha elections, where it secured over 18% of votes in Punjab compared with the SAD's over 13%, per reports. The SAD, once a dominant regional force, has seen declining fortunes after the Aam Aadmi Party swept to power in the state during the 2022 assembly elections.
items.title: BJP and SAD to Reunite in Punjab Ahead of Assembly Elections

visual.alt: Bar chart. BJP 18 %; SAD 13 %.

items.summary: At least four children were killed and 32 others injured after a speeding truck rammed into a stationary school bus on the Lucknow-Agra Expressway near Thathia area in Uttar Pradesh's Kannauj district around 6 am Tuesday, police said. The accident occurred when the Oriental Public School bus from Kaushambi was parked on the expressway shoulder to allow children to use the toilet; the truck struck it from behind and damaged its rear portion, according to Superintendent of Police Vinod Kumar. The bus was carrying 50 people, including students returning from an excursion to the Taj Mahal in Agra, with the injured group comprising eight school staff members and 24 students, police said. Responders—including police personnel, Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) staff, and passing commuters—rushed to the scene and rescued children from the damaged bus before they were taken by ambulance to a medical college where doctors declared four of them dead. The deceased were identified as Aryan Chaurasia (14), son of Prem Kumar Chaurasia; Raziullah (16), son of Shamiullah; and Armaan (17) and Zaid Mirza (17), both sons of Riaz Ahmad, according to police. School manager Salman and one child in critical condition were referred to Kanpur for further treatment while the remaining injured students and staff members are undergoing treatment at the medical college, Kumar said. District Magistrate Ashutosh Mohan Agnihotri and SP Kumar visited the medical college to inquire about the injured's conditions, police reported.
items.title: Truck Ramming Stationary School Bus Kills 4 Children, Injures 32 in Kannauj

items.summary: According to Hindustan Times reporting from its newsdesk, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal are expected to announce their alliance in Punjab today. The report is attributed to HT's round-the-clock newsdesk team, which covers Indian politics and elections through reporters on the ground as well as official statements and other authoritative sources, with stories subject to editorial scrutiny before publication.
items.title: BJP, Akali Dal Likely to Announce Punjab Alliance Today

items.summary: Speaking with Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi ahead of the release of her memoir Belonging: A Journey Of Love, Sonia Gandhi recounted why she declined to become Prime Minister after the Congress-led alliance won the 2004 Lok Sabha election. She said she felt responsible for party workers who had campaigned across India and believed leaving after the campaign would let them down, though she also questioned whether her sense of duty shaped that reasoning and reflected on how holding power can make it easy to find reasons to keep it. Rahul Gandhi described the atmosphere in the room when his mother decided against taking the post, noting one person present was seen as the strongest choice while others had hoped for the position; he said some felt relief from her decision while others were happy she stepped aside. The discussion took place around the release of Belonging: A Journey Of Love, which Sonia wrote from her own memories with Rahul and Priyanka adding their recollections to give the stories new life. Rahul also discussed episodes left out of the book, including abuse and humiliation his mother endured after joining the Nehru-Gandhi family, attacks on her because she was born in Italy despite efforts to settle into Indian life, allegations that Rajiv Gandhi's security removal was deliberate so he would be killed with a warning before his Bihar trip, and a failed proposal surrounding his seventh birthday. Sonia said revisiting those years brought back laughter, happiness, and painful memories while describing her children as her greatest joy and strength.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Recalls Turning Down 2004 PM Post in Memoir Discussion

items.summary: In a video interaction with his mother, Sonia Gandhi, and sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra while discussing her memoir 'Belonging,' Rahul Gandhi alleged that former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's security was deliberately removed so he could be killed. The remarks revived Congress's long-standing accusation against the then-V.P. Singh government regarding the withdrawal of Rajiv Gandhi's protection. During their discussion, Sonia Gandhi recounted how Rahul joined his father on a 1991 trip to Bihar where stones were pelted at him and anti-him slogans shouted by crowds; when Rahul returned home he told her that if nothing was done about his father's security, she would soon return for his funeral. Rahul described the Bihar incident as the final straw and stated clearly that 'Papa's security was removed so that he got killed,' adding that it was not an accident but deliberately created to enable his death. He also mentioned having argued with his father over his own security. Meanwhile, Priyanka recalled how after Indira Gandhi's assassination, Sonia became paranoid about Rajiv's security and would check the barbed wire and wake sleeping guards. The Congress party has maintained that the withdrawal of Rajiv Gandhi's security was an operation of law.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Alleges Rajiv Gandhi's Security Was Removed to Enable His Killing

items.summary: A vendor at the 13,000-foot-high Rohatang Pass in Himachal Pradesh reportedly generates daily sales of ₹14,000 to ₹15,000 from selling Maggi noodles and tea. According to the shopkeeper cited by content creator Harsh Chauhan—who shared a viral video discussing the business—the store sells about 60-70 plates of Maggi (priced at ₹100 each) and roughly 200 cups of tea (₹40 each) daily, yielding approximately ₹6,000 to ₹7,000 from Maggi and around ₹8,000 from tea. If this sales rate continued consistently, the monthly turnover could reach about ₹4.65 lakh; however, after deducting expenses for goods, transport, staff, and other costs, actual profit would be lower than gross sales.
items.title: Rohatang Pass Vendor's Daily Sales Surpass Monthly Figures in Himaachal Pradesh

visual.alt: Bar chart. Maggi Noodles 6,000 ₹; Tea 8,000 ₹.

items.summary: The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) of the Philippines has approved for public posting a draft resolution proposing a framework for imposing a Regional Secondary Price Cap (SPC) in the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM) Reserve Market. The proposed framework aims to establish a mechanism for applying secondary price caps across different regions in the country's electricity reserve market, with provisions specifically intended for the WESM Reserve Market. The Commission announced the development through a notice dated November 6, 2026, under ERC Case No. 2026-023 RM. The draft resolution, titled "A Resolution Adopting a Framework for the Imposition of a Regional Secondary Price Cap (SPC) in the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM) Reserve Market," was approved for publication on the Commission's official website. The proposed resolution includes an attached document outlining the Framework Governing the Secondary Price Cap for the Reserve Market, identified as Annex A. Interested parties and stakeholders have been invited to review the draft framework and submit their comments using the prescribed template provided in Annex B, with a deadline of November 13, 2026. As part of the consultation process, the ERC has scheduled a virtual public consultation for stakeholders from Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao on November 27, 2026, at 9:00 AM through the Microsoft Teams application. Interested participants seeking to attend are required to provide their respective email addresses to the Commission through legal.virtualhearings@erc.ph and mention the relevant case number, ERC Case No. 2026-023 RM; access links will be distributed within five working days before the scheduled consultation. The proposed framework is intended to establish regional secondary price cap provisions specifically for the WESM Reserve Market, with the consultation providing an opportunity for market participants and other interested stakeholders across the three major island groups to share their views on the proposed regulatory approach. According to the ERC notice, all comments received within the prescribed submission period will become part of the official records of the rulemaking proceeding and will be considered by the Commission while finalizing the resolution and adopting the framework for the regional Secondary Price Cap in the WESM Reserve Market.
items.title: Philippines ERC Proposes Regional Secondary Price Cap Framework for WESM Reserve Market

items.summary: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi alleged that the security of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi was deliberately withdrawn in order to facilitate his killing. She made the remarks during a conversation with her children, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, about her book Belonging: A Journey of Love.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Alleges Rajiv Gandhi's Security Was Deliberately Withdrawn to Facilitate His Killing

items.summary: Kerala Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan said on Tuesday that a drop in Sabarimala pilgrims this year was caused by problems in the virtual queue booking system, with suspicions that slots were being booked in bulk and sold illegally. He stated that around 6,000 devotees per day are not showing up despite having secured bookings through the virtual queue. In response to these no-shows, Muraleedharan said instructions have been given to increase spot booking slots, though this requires approval from the Kerala High Court; he noted that permission has already been sought by the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB). The minister added that the TDB is examining the matter and had sent a letter to State Home Minister asking them to investigate all aspects of suspected illegal slot sales, warning that anyone caught selling bookings illegally will face stringent action. He assured reporters that the identified booking system problem would be examined and resolved, while noting separately that devotees are turning up in greater numbers than usual during monthly poojas at the hill-top shrine.
items.title: Sabarimala Pilgrim Drop Attributed to Booking System Issues

items.summary:
Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM) has revised its billing methodology for High Tension (HT) consumers using wheeled solar and non-solar power under the Open Access regime. The revision, announced in a circular dated November 12, 2026, directs field officers to use a sequential allocation method for wheeled solar energy instead of the previously used ratio-based approach. This change is based on the KERC Tariff Order dated March 27, 2025, and the KERC (Terms and Conditions for Open Access) Regulations dated March 26, 2025.

Under the applicable framework, HT electricity consumption is classified into four Time of Day (ToD) slots: morning peak hours from 06:00 to 09:00, day off-peak hours from 09:00 to 18:00, evening peak hours from 18:00 to 22:00, and night off-peak hours from 22:00 to 06:00 the following day. Because solar generation generally occurs between 09:00 and 15:00, wheeled solar electricity falls entirely within daytime off-peak hours. The Open Access regulations permit banked off-peak energy to be adjusted only against off-peak consumption; it cannot offset morning or evening peak-hour usage.

BESCOM found that the earlier ratio-based method distributed wheeled solar and non-solar energy across all four ToD slots according to their share of total monthly consumption. This allowed some solar energy to be adjusted against peak-hour consumption, contrary to regulatory provisions, understating BESCOM's electricity supply during peak hours and affecting applicable Time of Day (ToD) charges.

Under the revised procedure, wheeled solar energy must first be allocated to daytime off-peak consumption, followed by night off-peak consumption. Allocation in each slot is limited to actual metered consumption recorded during that period. Any remaining solar energy after meeting both off-peak slots cannot be adjusted against peak-hour consumption and will be treated as BESCOM-supplied energy. Wheeled non-solar energy is allocated thereafter, with any remaining demand billed as BESCOM supply along with applicable ToD and Open Access charges.

BESCOM's illustrative calculation demonstrates the impact of the change for a consumer with 56,00,790 metered units, 40,00,000 wheeled solar units, and 15,95,000 wheeled non-solar units. Under the earlier method, 11,50,616 solar units were incorrectly adjusted against peak slots. Under the revised method, 20,32,920 solar units are allocated to daytime off-peak consumption and 19,56,780 units to night off-peak consumption. The remaining 10,300 solar units cannot be adjusted, increasing total BESCOM-billed energy by 16,090 units.

The revised methodology will apply from the December 2026 billing month. BESCOM has instructed field offices to review and correct previously issued non-compliant bills and update HT billing software to implement the new allocation procedure.
items.title: BESCOM Revises Solar Open Access Billing Rules For HT Consumers From December 2026

items.summary: Saurav Das, co-convener of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), alleged that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from boarding a 1 am flight to London after his passport was flagged. According to news agency Press Trust of India (PTI), Das said he had been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union to participate in a panel discussion about the "cockroach movement" and claimed several other universities, including Cambridge, LSE, and Edinburgh, also extended invitations for him to speak on the topic. In posts on X, Das accused the Narendra Modi government of preventing his travel, stating he was invited by prestigious institutions but denied permission to attend events discussing the cockroach movement. He questioned why the government would object to an educated young person participating in intellectual discussions at international universities and criticized the administration's functioning, including its inability to expand the cabinet due to ministers refusing to resign. Das also attacked fugitive businessmen Nirav Modi and Vijay Mallya while criticizing the alleged action. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke similarly condemned the incident on X, suggesting that someone in power was jealous of Das receiving an invitation from Oxford. Despite being unable to board his scheduled flight, Das said he would not be discouraged from continuing his work and intended to travel to London, Paris, and other international destinations in the future. The report does not include a response from the government or immigration authorities regarding the alleged passport flagging.
items.title: Cockroach Janta Party's Saurav Das Alleges Delhi Airport Passport Flagging Blocked London Trip

items.summary: At a high-level United Nations Security Council briefing on Monday, India's Permanent Representative Harish Parvathaneni called for an immediate halt to attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Black Sea, saying safe navigation through international waterways must be restored at the earliest. Speaking of the Russia-Ukraine conflict now in its fifth year, he said it was having far-reaching consequences due to interconnected global supply chains, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi noting that "the world has to move from 'endless war to the end of war.'" Parvathaneni emphasized that conflicts exacerbate food insecurity by disrupting agriculture and hindering humanitarian access, with consequences extending through energy, fertiliser, transport and agricultural trade while disproportionately impacting the Global South. He highlighted the Black Sea region's importance to global food security, noting that the region combined with India accounted for almost a fifth of global cereal production (3 million people; 04), and that Russia and Ukraine together accounted for nearly a quarter of global exports of wheat, maize and barley. The envoy cited India's humanitarian assistance—wheat supplies to Afghanistan, rice to Sudan, and aid to Palestine—and referenced External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar's observation at the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting that fertiliser shortages stem partly from the Black Sea and partly from the Gulf and Red Sea. Recalling the 1943 Bengal famine that killed over three million people in India, Parvathaneni stressed the human cost of distant conflicts. He detailed attacks on merchant vessels: the MV Omorfi attacked on 18 July with an Indian crew member lost; the MV Royad Mammadov under attack in October with three Indian nationals aboard; and two additional ships (MV Golden Leo and MV AGN RAGNAR) struck, resulting in four dead and two missing Indian seafarers. He thanked partner countries for repatriating injured seafarers while reiterating the call to end targeting of commercial shipping and restore safe navigation.
items.title: India Urges UN Security Council to End Black Sea Shipping Attacks and Restore Safe Navigation

items.summary: AI investing startup Supertake has raised $20 million in seed funding, led by venture firm Adjacent (Nico Wittenborn), with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Union Square Ventures (USV). Numerous angel investors also joined the round, including Nat Friedman of Meta Superintelligence Labs, Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch, product manager Nikita Bier, investor Scott Belsky, and Nemil Dalal. The company lets users turn their market ideas into real investment portfolios using frontier AI models and trading agents; Supertake's users' ideas are tracked on a leaderboard so others who agree can invest alongside them.
items.title: Supertake Raises $20M Seed to Turn Market Predictions Into Stock Portfolios

items.summary: Demonstrators rallied in Brussels carrying placards warning that 'Rent is eating into our wages' and 'The rich earn more, the workers pay more,' to oppose around €10 billion in proposed spending cuts before clashes broke out with riot police. Officers responded with tear gas, water cannons, and charges as a car burned and arrests were made amid plumes of smoke. For protesters already squeezed by high energy costs, inflation, and shrinking purchasing power, the planned savings threaten to place an unfair burden on the lowest-paid while undermining social security, employment support, and help for families. The street anger occurred on the very day Prime Minister Bart De Wever met King Philippe to update him on strained talks over Belgium's 2027 budget. Having set a year-end deadline for coalition partners to sign off on the cuts and warned that the government could collapse if negotiations fail, De Wever now faces sharpening resistance both inside parliament and on the streets as he seeks to reconcile fiscal discipline with demands to protect living standards.
items.title: Belgian Workers March Against Spending Cuts Amid Rising Living Costs

items.summary:
Los Angeles' long-awaited LAX people mover project, officially named SkyLink, has gone off track despite its elevated tracks and train cars being operational. The less than 2.5 miles (4km) rail line broke ground in 2019 under then-mayor Eric Garcetti as part of a $30bn plan to modernize LAX, aiming to provide direct terminal-to-terminal connections with congestion relief for the airport's millions of annual visitors.

The project has exceeded its budget by more than $1bn and is expected to overshoot its intended 2023 opening date by four years. City officials report it is 99% complete, but final testing requiring at least 30 consecutive days of uninterrupted operation has stretched beyond 200 days. An estimated opening was pushed back multiple times to March 2027 after Linxs moved the projected date again last week.

The project began as a public-private partnership between Los Angeles World Airports (Lawa) and contractor LAX Integrated Express Solutions (Linxs), which signed a contract in 2019 to design, construct, operate and maintain SkyLink for 30 years. The initial price tag was $1.9bn; disputes over design codes led Linxs to submit hundreds of change orders, culminating in a settlement granting an additional $550m as costs ballooned to nearly $3bn.

A Los Angeles county civil grand jury released its report last year concluding that Linxs took the airport authority for about $880m because city officials wrote up the contract poorly. The contractor allegedly leveraged contractual intricacies by barraging departments with change orders and delaying work, while also using political pressure around major sporting events as leverage.

In July, Linxs sued the city over alleged breaches of contract including faulty electrical equipment that delayed key testing more than 140 days, though airport officials called these false legal assertions. Under settlement terms, Linxs must deliver a passenger-ready system by December 8; if it misses this date, which appears likely to happen, the project could face further disarray.

Eli Lipmen of Move LA described the project as an embarrassment and warned of potentially having a $3bn distressed asset on their hands. Nithya Raman, who defeated incumbent mayor Karen Bass in the mayoral race, held up SkyLink as a symbol of city hall dysfunction and called for investigation into alleged criminal wrongdoing.

The 11-acre LAX/Metro Transit Center opened June 2025 but remains separate from the people mover. UCLA's Juan Matute intends to study how this public-private partnership derailed, noting that outside oversight could help prevent similar mistakes in future projects.
items.title: LAX's SkyLink People Mover Derailed by Delays, Cost Overruns

items.summary: Tensions are escalating in Libya after an attack on two vessels off the coast of Benghazi, one of which was a Russian warship. Naval forces in eastern Libya have been placed on maximum alert following the incident. Kyiv claims to have carried out an operation targeting Russian military assets, while the United Nations is calling for an independent investigation and warning that the Russia-Ukraine conflict could expand onto Libyan soil. Separately, China has increased its diplomatic engagement in the Horn of Africa amid growing tensions in the Red Sea and Middle East; Chinese envoys traveled to Ethiopia, Djibouti, Egypt, and Eritrea to promote dialogue, regional security, and cooperation among countries in the region. On the climate front, COP31 concluded in Turkey without a major agreement after negotiations stalled over fossil fuels, climate finance, and carbon capture, renewing calls for reform of a process widely seen as paralysed by its consensus rule. In Central Africa, efforts are underway to ease tensions between Nairobi and Kinshasa; Kenyan President William Ruto and DR Congo's President Félix Tshisekedi met in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, under the mediation of Denis Sassou-Nguesso, with both leaders pledging to prioritise dialogue and strengthen economic and healthcare cooperation. In Cairo, an annual honey festival is celebrating Egyptian producers while raising awareness about different varieties; the sector is expanding, with more than 20,000 tonnes produced this year and several thousand tonnes exported.
items.title: Russia Claims Attack on Libyan Vessels Including Warship; COP31 Ends Without Major Agreement

items.summary: Subaru is introducing front-wheel-drive (FWD) variants on select electric models as a cost-cutting measure, starting with the Uncharted EV. The 2027 Uncharted EV Premium FWD model features a single 221-horsepower front-mounted motor and starts at $34,995 in the US; higher-priced Sport ($39,795) and GT ($43,795) trims retain Subaru's Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive with X-Mode for combined 338 horsepower. The Uncharted was the first Subaru model in about 30 years not to come standard with all-wheel drive. In contrast, the larger US-market Solterra and Trailseeker EVs remain AWD-only, starting at $38,495 and $39,995 respectively. Meanwhile, Subaru opened preorders for its new 2027 electric range in Spain—including the Uncharted (starting €26,525/$28,900), Solterra (€35,025/$38,200), and E-Outback/Trailseeker (€36,525/$39,800)—all offered with lower-priced FWD variants while retaining AWD on higher trims. The Solterra and E-Outback are expected to launch in mid-2027. Electrek noted that the Uncharted remains Subaru's only EV sold with standard FWD, though it speculated a FWD option could later reach other models like the Solterra; AWD is used more heavily in the US than in Spain.
items.title: Subaru Adds Front-Wheel-Drive Versions to Cut EV Prices

items.summary: On Monday (23 November 2026), UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that artificial intelligence is advancing at extraordinary speed and amplifying cybersecurity risks, manipulation, and misuse, while urging countries to act now so every nation can manage the technology safely. Speaking at a news conference during the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety in Barbados, Guterres said recent technological outages and cyberattacks have exposed vulnerabilities in digital systems that societies increasingly depend on, noting that protections remain fragmented and too often reactive. He emphasized that many countries still lack the tools, knowledge, and capacity to assess AI systems entering their markets or protect people when problems arise, calling this gap a priority that must be closed so every country can manage AI safely with credible, independent ways to evaluate powerful AI systems. Guterres urged states, the private sector, financial institutions, foundations, and other donors to increase investments in AI capacity-building and contribute urgently to funding for developing minimum AI capacity in Global South regions, stressing that because risks are global, responses must be global. Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley echoed the call, warning that if AI capacity remains concentrated in a few regions existing inequalities would widen further; she pointed to needed investments in infrastructure, data sets, skills, and models respecting local values, saying AI innovation must advance human rights, support sustainable development, enable people's agency over their future, reflect global diversity, build locally for sovereignty, and avoid the commoditization of human beings as data packs serving only a few.
items.title: UN Chief Warns AI Risks Growing as He Urges Global Action to Close Capacity Gap

items.summary: In the 2026 midterm elections, Democrats won the U.S. House by their largest margin in half a century and secured the biggest majority since the early 1990s. Fifty-six percent of voters chose Democratic candidates compared with 42% for Republicans, producing a 14-point gap that NPR identified as the widest such advantage in 50 years.
items.title: Democrats Win Largest House Majority in 50 Years as COP31 Ends Without a Deal

items.summary: Hours before Nvidia reinstated ousted CEO Jensen Huang, President Donald Trump called into the company's Sunday board meeting to argue for his return. The direct engagement by Trump — first reported by Semafor and confirmed by multiple sources — underscores how he has redefined the role of the US government in private enterprise. Vice President JD Vance and other administration members also became involved in Nvidia's inner workings, even as some members of Trump's own party questioned whether reinstating Huang poses a national security risk.
items.title: Trump Pressured Nvidia Board to Reinstated Jensen Huang

items.summary: High street retailer Next announced that some of its data has been accessed in a cyber breach affecting a third-party online supplier. The company, headquartered in Enderby, Leicestershire, said it was informed by the supplier about an incident involving "unauthorised access to certain benign data relating to Next." Next stated there was no evidence that customers' personal data had been compromised and described the affected information as limited in nature, concluding that based on its current assessment it cannot be used to facilitate fraud against customers or the company. The firm said it took immediate steps to investigate the incident with the supplier while investigations continued, treating the situation "with the utmost seriousness" and working with the supplier, police, and regulators.
items.title: Next Reports Cyber Breach at Third-Party Supplier

items.summary:
Balendra Shah, a 36-year-old rapper-turned-politician and Nepal's first-time prime minister, made his inaugural state visit to India this week, marking a departure from the country's history of revolving coalition governments. As a young leader with a strong electoral mandate, Shah represents a new political force in Kathmandu whose bilateral trip carried significant weight given long-standing economic strain, August's devastating flash floods, and public hopes for jobs, investment, and better governance.

Shah prioritized securing Indian support to safeguard Nepal's flood recovery. The August disaster claimed more than 1,450 lives, with 5,745 people missing or unaccounted for. The floods swept away roads, bridges, hydropower projects, and settlements, leaving reconstruction bills estimated at around $4.8 billion (about €4.4 billion). At a joint press briefing after talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, Modi announced a $1.63 billion package to help rebuild flood-hit areas and upgrade infrastructure — roughly $380 million as a grant, with the remainder as a concessional loan.

The two countries agreed to deepen cooperation across trade, investment, connectivity, people-to-people ties, educational and innovation partnerships, energy and infrastructure collaboration, market access, and additional air and port access for landlocked Nepal. They also launched a new long-term vision aimed at strengthening economic integration and development.

Despite the focus on economics, unresolved territorial disputes persist over Kalapani, Lipulekh, and Limpiyadhura in northwestern Nepal. As mayor of Kathmandu, Shah raised these border issues to boost his nationalist image; however, his India visit steered clear of such contentious matters. Bimala Rai Paudyal, a former Foreign Minister of Nepal, told DW that while the visit could be a good starting point for resolving border issues, "the new government didn't show interest or the guts to address this." Ashok Swain, head of the Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Sweden's Uppsala University, added that Nepal's territorial disputes, concerns over the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, and its economic and transit dependence on India need addressing. He argued Shah's biggest opportunity is to transform Nepal's location between India and China from a strategic vulnerability into an economic and diplomatic asset.

Constantino Xavier, a senior fellow at the Center for Social and Economic Progress in New Delhi, cautioned against expecting too much from a single visit, telling DW that "we need a big, long-term ambition coupled with small, short-term steps" while keeping economic cooperation central to relations. Whether the visit marks a tangible reset on the economic front will ultimately depend not on the number of agreements announced but on how they are implemented and whether both governments address the disputes that have long strained ties.
items.title: Nepal's New PM Balendra Shah Eyes Closer Ties with India Amid Lingering Disputes

items.summary: The article examines whether battery storage will displace gas-fired turbines in electricity markets, arguing that while wholesale price undercutting is occurring—evidenced by California using gas-fired combustion turbines less as batteries underprice them—the disruption to fossil generation may be overstated. According to the EIA, US capacity additions are projected at 86 GW for 2026, with solar and battery accounting for 89% of that growth versus only 7% from gas-fired sources; 2025 additions were similar in fuel mix. The authors contend that despite rising demand—attributed to AI—the apparent stability of gas-fueled electricity production suggests fossil generation will coexist with renewables in the near and intermediate term, likening this dynamic to how telegraph and telephone technologies coexisted for decades before one replaced the other.
items.title: Will Batteries Kill Off Gas Turbines at Data Centers

visual.alt: Bar chart. Solar and battery 89 %; Gas-fired 7 %.

items.summary: A judiciary official said Monday that Iranian courts have ordered the United States to pay $290 billion in damages for decades of actions against Iran. Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary's centre for lawyers, told state television: "We have secured court rulings in domestic courts awarding $290 billion in damages against the Americans." According to state TV, the ruling covers US actions going back decades.
items.title: Iranian Courts Order US to Pay $290 Billion in Damages

items.summary: On November 24, Alibaba rejected the addition of its subsidiary Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) to a United States trade blacklist, calling it an "erroneous" move. In a statement provided to The Straits Times, an Alibaba spokesperson said that adding Apex to the Entity List is erroneous because "Apex has never diverted advanced computing chips subject to US export restrictions," and added that the company will pursue all legal avenues to protect its rights and reputation. Apex was one of seven companies added on November 23 to an entity list managed by the United States Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which said the firms were "determined by the US government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States." Singapore-based Megaspeed International, at the centre of investigations into possible diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China, was the primary target; its parent company Swiftdata and Malaysian subsidiaries MSFusion, Speedmatrix and Megaspeed International, plus Thai subsidiary Megaspeed (Thailand), were also blacklisted. Corporate records obtained by The Straits Times earlier in November showed Apex had an active financial arrangement with Speedmatrix under a June 18, 2024 agreement pledging specified IT and network equipment, intellectual property and related rights as security for contractual obligations; corporate records also show Apex was incorporated in Singapore in July 2023 at Lazada One on Bras Basah Road, leased by Alibaba and its Southeast Asian online shopping unit Lazada Group. Alibaba's immediate holding company is Cloud Intelligence (Cayman) Holding, with ultimate control held by Cayman Islands-incorporated Alibaba Group Holding, which holds contractual rights to Alibaba China's profits.
items.title: Alibaba Rejects US Blacklisting of Singapore Chip-Rerouting Subsidiary

items.summary: As of September 30, 2026, HDFC Bank topped the list of stocks with the highest domestic institutional investor (DII) holdings at Rs 4,13,340 crore, though its market capitalisation stood at Rs 10,68,200 crore. ICICI Bank ranked second with DII holdings worth Rs 3,98,477 crore and a market capitalisation of Rs 10,00,861 crore. Reliance Industries placed third with domestic institutional investors holding shares valued at Rs 3,44,678 crore against a market capitalisation of Rs 16,10,372 crore. Bharti Airtel featured fourth with DII holdings worth Rs 2,38,345 crore and a market capitalisation of Rs 11,80,889 crore. State Bank of India ranked fifth with domestic institutional investors holding shares valued at Rs 2,31,661 crore against a market capitalisation of Rs 8,84,861 crore. Larsen & Toubro secured sixth place with DII holdings worth Rs 2,21,145 crore and a market capitalisation of Rs 5,01,789 crore. Axis Bank ranked seventh with domestic institutional investors holding shares valued at Rs 1,70,025 crore against a market capitalisation of Rs 3,79,092 crore. Kotak Mahindra Bank featured eighth with DII holdings worth Rs 1,59,380 crore and a market capitalisation of Rs 4,28,256 crore. Infosys placed ninth with domestic institutional investors holding shares valued at Rs 1,58,365 crore against a market capitalisation of Rs 4,68,244 crore. items.title: HDFC Bank Leads Top 10 Stocks by Domestic Institutional Investor Holdings in Q2

items.summary:
Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO triggered a sharp rally across Asia-Pacific markets, with the Taiwanese TW50 index up 9.5%, South Korea's Kospi jumping 6.5% (led by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics), Tokyo's Nikkei gaining nearly 4%, and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rising 1.8%. This followed a Wall Street surge where Nvidia shares jumped 31.5%, adding roughly $950bn to the company's value as Huang returned to headquarters, marking Wall Street's best day since April 2025 when Trump paused his Liberation Day tariffs. Saxo chief investment strategist Charu Chanana attributed part of the rally to Huang's return removing uncertainty and restoring strategic continuity at Nvidia.

Despite the optimism, doubts persisted over AI companies' high valuations and whether they could generate revenues to sustain heavy data center spending. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index dipped 0.73%, which AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould suggested may reflect fears of a clampdown on US AI chip exports once the initial excitement faded.

Political backlash intensified, with Democrat Senator Elizabeth Warren calling Huang's restoration "reckless" and warning her upcoming banking committee would investigate whether Nvidia complied with export controls, while demanding Congress be told what input government officials gave to support his reinstatement. Republican lawmakers also criticized the board decision; Nebraska Senator Pete Ricketts wrote on X that Huang's behavior did not support reinstatement amid allegations of an affair with a Chinese spy.

Trump had reportedly dialed into Nvidia's Sunday board meeting before the announcement, arguing for Huang's return and asking Vice President JD Vance to work with the board to assure them Huang was not a national security risk. House Oversight Committee top Democrat Robert Garcia said Trump's direct involvement raised "serious national security and corruption questions," demanding swift bipartisan action.

Trump's Nvidia holdings rose in value by as much as $15m (£11.5m) on Monday, with his total stock position valued between $11m (£8.4m) and $55m (£42.1m), per the FT citing a Reuters review of disclosure filings.

Germany's foreign minister Johann Wadephul told AFP he was "shocked" by Trump's intervention to reinstate Huang, noting he had never seen such political interference in a company before. Chinese state media warned Beijing and Washington tensions would not end with Huang's return; Global Times urged China to remain vigilant against renewed export license delays and congressional hearings.

The Commerce Department added Megaspeed International to its trade blacklist on Monday, barring it from buying advanced AI chips without approval—a move that revealed Huang's relationship with Megaspeed founder Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Huang returned to Nvidia HQ wearing his signature dark uniform as employees chanted "Jensen, Jensen, Jensen," vowing to be a better CEO.

European markets showed less enthusiasm; London's FTSE 100 dipped 5 points (0.05%) to 10,475 after already rising 1.3% on Monday following the announcement. Swissquote senior analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya noted Huang's return would not ease broader AI risks including massive infrastructure spending and hyperscaler free cash flow pressure.

Analysts offered mixed outlooks: UniCredit Munich strategist Christian Stocker said investors were re-engaging with the AI theme on relief that supply chain disruption was unlikely, while DeutscheBank's Jim Reid argued markets now priced in a more hawkish Federal Reserve path—with 25bp hike fully expected at December's meeting (26.1bps total, +3.1bps intraday) and 70bps of hikes by September 2027 (+6.6bps).
items.title: Nvidia shares fall in premarket trading as Jensen Huang’s return sparks US political backlash

items.summary:
Donald Trump reportedly made up to $15m (£11.5m) on his Nvidia holdings after the chipmaker's shares surged following the reinstatement of co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, according to a report by The Item. Huang was ousted from Nvidia in 2024 amid allegations involving three affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with employees, but the board brought him back after an intervention Trump described on CNBC as convincing them he "made the deal." Financial disclosures filed with the Office of Government Ethics indicate Trump may have owned up to 370,000 Nvidia shares as of September 30, per data first reported by the Financial Times. The president's holdings in Nvidia range between $23m and $86m over two years according to a BBC review; he has sold part of his stake since returning to office and gained between $3.5m and $10.2m on those trades, per government disclosures.

Nvidia shares jumped 31.5% in Monday's trading, adding roughly $950bn to the company's value as Huang returned to Santa Clara headquarters amid a crowd of employees chanting his name. The rally extended across Asia-Pacific markets Tuesday: Taiwan's TW50 index rose 9.5%, South Korea's Kospi climbed 6.5% led by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, and Japan's Nikkei gained nearly 4%, while European markets were broadly flat. Nvidia shares then fell 4.1% in premarket trading to $158.26 as traders weighed political backlash over Huang's return; US markets are expected to open slightly lower Tuesday after Monday's gains.

The volatility reflects broader AI-sector concerns about high debt levels funding infrastructure buildouts and potential tougher regulation following the Democrats' midterm victory. Senator Ruben Gallego (D-Arizona) called for an investigation into stock positions before Huang's announcement, calling the White House "the most corrupt in history" and suggesting Trump may have started popping the AI bubble; Roger Lee of Cavendish questioned whether technology CEOs like Huang are now too systemically important to be fired. Economists noted Huang's return reduced fears of an imminent AI-bubble burst, making a rate hike more likely: Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid said markets were once again pricing in a 25 basis point Federal Reserve increase at the December meeting.
items.title: Trump Made Up to $15m on Nvidia Stock After Jensen Huang's Return

items.summary: Nearly two weeks after Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive of Nvidia, the Taiwanese-American tech billionaire was reinstated on Monday (Nov 23), sending Nvidia shares soaring 31.5 per cent in a day and reviving investor interest across AI-related stocks. The comeback followed revelations that had plunged the chipmaker into crisis: reports of extramarital affairs—including one with Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy—and mounting pressure from US President Donald Trump, industry figures like Tesla CEO Elon Musk, and prominent venture capitalists who signed an online petition drawing over 180,000 signatures. In his statement, Huang said he was honored to return and 'can't wait to get back to work,' while videos circulating on social media showed him wearing a navy jacket instead of his signature black leather jacket with his hand over his heart amid cheers from employees across multiple floors; he added that he would be 'a better CEO the second time around.' The timeline traces how the controversy unfolded, beginning Oct 29 when the New York Times reported US authorities investigated Alice Huang for allegedly passing intelligence to Beijing and helping circumvent restrictions on advanced AI chips—after which Nvidia's closing share price fell to US$213.66 (0.8 per cent down from Oct 28). On Oct 30, the Wall Street Journal alleged Alice Huang had links to Chinese intelligence, prompting Singapore officials' concerns; that day Huang told Bloomberg News his dealings with Megaspeed were 'normal and not unusual,' while Beijing dismissed the espionage claims as 'groundless speculation.' Trump voiced support on Oct 31, calling Huang 'brilliant' and saying Washington was looking 'very closely' at the issue. On Nov 4 to Nov 5, three senior Republican lawmakers requested a closed-door briefing from Huang over the intelligence allegations; Nvidia responded that its cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information rather than sensitive trade secrets or national security data, with closing shares falling to US$181.60 (9.3 per cent down from Nov 4). On Nov 8, Huang admitted his infidelity in a message to employees, taking 'full responsibility' while remaining committed to Nvidia and supporting the independent investigation; following this admission, Nvidia announced its board was launching an inquiry into whether Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence—though shares had already dropped about US$190 billion off market value—and closed at US$186.64 on Friday (Nov 6), up 2.8 per cent from Nov 5. On Nov 9, Trump defended Huang as an 'honorable guy' who had not discussed the affair allegations with him; Chinese officials again dismissed espionage claims during a press briefing, and Nvidia's closing share price fell to US$178.67 (4.3 per cent down from Nov 6). On Nov 10, The Associated Press reported that a shareholder sued Nvidia and Huang for deceiving investors about the affair and Megaspeed; shares closed at US$168.89 (5.5 per cent down from Nov 9). On Nov 11, the New York Times reported an alleged second affair with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care—while unconfirmed, this sent Nvidia shares falling nearly 4 per cent in extended trading; closing price rose to US$173.73 (2.9 per cent up from Nov 10). On Nov 12, Huang announced his resignation as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress taking over as interim chief executive and longtime engineer Ian Buck emerging as a leading internal candidate. On Nov 13, US lawmakers summoned Huang to face questions in December after the scandal had wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market valuation; Senator Tim Scott requested testimony before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec 1, while Huang faced closed-door interviews with three House committees under threat of subpoena—closing shares fell to US$162.85 (2 per cent down from Nov 12). On Nov 16, citing people familiar with the matter, the Financial Times reported Huang was considering a comeback as CEO; sources said Silicon Valley executives were assembling a 'war room' to lobby for his return and garner White House support, while Trump told reporters he would welcome Huang's return. However, on Nov 17, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said the board did not intend to reinstate Huang despite his readiness to return—though Nvidia doubled its revenue in Q3 to more than US$115 billion, exceeding analysts' expectations; closing shares fell slightly to US$155.46 (0.4 per cent down from Nov 16). On Nov 20, Anthropic's record US$81 billion listing failed to arrest Nvidia's slide amid worries about the sector's investments and valuations, while Trump again praised Huang as 'a good man' who should be given a second chance; closing shares fell sharply to US$125.53 (14 per cent down from Nov 19). Finally on Nov 23, Nvidia's board reinstated Huang in a surprise move after late Sunday discussions that even interim CEO Colette Kress was unaware of—Jones said the board believed Jensen 'is the right person to lead Nvidia' and his return serves stockholders; despite gaining nearly US$1 trillion in market value, Nvidia remained worth about a fifth less than a month earlier.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Stunning Return as Nvidia CEO: A Timeline of Events

items.summary: The Nvidia board reinstated Jensen Huang to the CEO position, a move that boosted Nvidia's share price by about a third. According to the article, this decision followed a phone call from someone in the White House—possibly Donald Trump himself—who reportedly told the board there was nothing to worry about regarding stories concerning Huang's relationship with Alice Huang and an alleged connection to China. The article draws parallels between Huang's reinstatement and Sam Altman being fired by OpenAI only to be reinstated within weeks following investor pressure, suggesting Silicon Valley has developed a tendency to treat company founders as untouchable figures. Trump stated that the board asked whether there was a national security problem and he responded 'No, it's not a problem.' The article frames this episode as evidence of growing corporate power in the AI era, comparing current tech leaders—described as Huangs, Altmans, Musks, Amodeis, and Zuckerbergs—to Gilded Age industrialists like Vanderbilt, Carnegie, Rockefeller, and Morgan. It notes that during 1913, the richest 1% of taxpayers drew almost 18% of the nation's income and held nearly 40% of the nation's wealth—shares similar to what they hold today—and by the late 1970s this figure had fallen below a quarter. The article references President Rutherford B. Hayes writing in his diary that 'This is a government of corporations, by corporations, and for corporations,' echoing Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg address.
items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after White House intervention

items.summary: Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO, an event that became the top trending post on Weibo and is being described by some observers as one of the greatest U-turns of all time. Chinese state media dismissed claims that a woman connected to Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security as a spy, framing the saga instead as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington; The Global Times called it a 'witch hunt.' Meanwhile, the White House and President Donald Trump have said Huang poses no national security threat, though investigations into the allegations remain ongoing. Observers note that Huang's reappointment came shortly after Xi Jinping met with Trump in Shenzhen last week, raising questions about whether direct engagement influences Washington; Trump confirmed the two discussed Huang but did not elaborate further, while Beijing has not commented. The episode reinforced a view among Chinese officials of two camps in Washington regarding export controls on advanced technology. Although Huang argues that US restrictions will push firms like Huawei to build independent alternatives, his return is seen as no guarantee of relief for China because chip sales remain contentious ahead of an expected Trump-Xi meeting in December. New rules from the Bureau of Industry and Security are tightening restrictions by targeting not only direct exports but also Chinese firms' ability to use computing power overseas through cloud providers in countries like Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand; China has yet to react with measures of its own. Investors will watch for escalation that could weigh on US equity markets, as Trump's willingness to intervene in Nvidia's leadership decisions is seen by some observers as leverage given his concern about the stock market. Trump has personally invested in Nvidia, though the White House emphasized he placed his businesses in a trust managed by his sons. China previously used its rare earth metals chokehold to bring the US to trade negotiations; if chip export restrictions and Chinese retaliation escalate, that could affect markets because American companies rely on rare earths for products from cars to defense systems. Observers note more trouble lies ahead as China pursues what it describes as a 'constructive strategic relationship' with the US over control of critical technology and minerals affecting military influence and economic power. Huang is set to testify before Congress next month, and a Democrat-controlled Congress will raise pressure in January; Arkansas senator Tom Cotton wrote on X that the Nvidia controversy 'is just the tip of the iceberg.'
items.title: Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia CEO Role Sparks Reflections in China

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India approved South Indian Bank Limited (SIBL)'s acquisition by SBI Mutual Fund, a subsidiary of State Bank of India. The approval was communicated to the bank on November 23 and is subject to compliance with applicable regulatory conditions. According to a filing from South Indian Bank, the RBI has permitted SBI Mutual Fund to acquire an aggregate holding of up to 9.99 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights in the bank, subject to specified conditions. The approval is contingent on compliance with the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; the RBI's Directions on Acquisition and Holding of Shares or Voting Rights in Commercial Banks, 2025; the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999; and other applicable laws and regulatory guidelines.
items.title: RBI Approves SBI Mutual Fund's Stake in South Indian Bank

items.summary: On November 23, Nvidia's board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer effective immediately, reinstating him as a board member after reversing its earlier decision on his departure. The company said the board was satisfied with Huang's candor and leadership capabilities during discussions that followed his resignation, and it consulted senior US government officials before concluding his return posed no national security risk. Board Chair Harvey C. Jones stated Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia and that reinstatement serves shareholders, employees, partners and customers; he will remain board chair while Colette Kress continues as chief financial officer after serving as interim CEO during Huang's absence. Huang had voluntarily resigned on November 12 after the board raised concerns about his personal conduct being inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and corporate culture. On Nvidia's quarterly earnings call on November 17, Jones said the board unanimously accepted the resignation and did not intend to reinstate Huang, prompting Kress to become interim CEO as the company searched for a permanent successor. The reversal followed public support for Huang's return, including a Reuters report that a petition had attracted more than 180,000 signatures with one from Tesla CEO Elon Musk, while President Donald Trump—who urged Nvidia to bring Huang back—welcomed the decision on Truth Social and said the US government saw no national security risk. Despite his return, an independent investigation launched by the board will continue through completion with Huang pledging full cooperation; Nvidia has also established a separate National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors overseeing trade compliance while seeking to appoint a chief compliance officer.
items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Board Reversal

items.summary: US President Donald Trump said he spoke directly with Nvidia's board before the reinstatement of chief executive Jensen Huang, who had resigned less than two weeks earlier amid a scandal involving an alleged affair with a woman suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence. In an interview with CNBC on Monday, Trump explained that he contacted board members because he considered Nvidia strategically important to the United States and described finding "the board to be very, very reasonable." Separately, Nvidia announced on Monday that its board had unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately. The decision followed an initial statement from the board indicating it did not intend to bring Huang back, despite his expressed willingness to return.
items.title: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Intervention

items.summary: According to a Wall Street Journal report, Nvidia's co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang admitted before the company's board that he had more than three alleged affairs beyond those already reported. The 63-year-old reportedly expressed regret over his behavior during Sunday's lengthy board meeting, in which members spoke with him for several hours about undisclosed private relationships and explained the importance of transparency and honesty. Although these claims have not been independently verified, the board decided on Monday to reinstate Huang as CEO. The dispute reportedly began when reports emerged that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an official at Singapore's Megaspeed company who U.S. authorities accuse of spying for China; China has dismissed those accusations as baseless. Earlier reporting by the New York Times and Reuters also raised questions about other alleged private relationships involving Huang. Following his reinstatement announcement on Monday, Nvidia employees greeted him with applause in a video from its headquarters in Santa Clara, California, while an online petition supporting his return reportedly gathered thousands of signatures. The report claims that U.S. President Donald Trump and several tech-industry figures backed the decision to bring Huang back.
items.title: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang After Private-Relationship Confession, Shares Jump
